---
title: "Co-enrichment"
description: "Compare functional enrichment signals across multiple protein or result sets."
---

## Purpose

Co-enrichment is useful when several contrasts, omics layers, tissues, or protein clusters have already been analyzed and you want to distinguish **shared functional themes** from **condition-specific terms**.

## Recommended inputs

Use enrichment result sets derived from compatible identifier/background systems. If two analyses used different gene universes or incompatible annotation versions, direct comparison of p-values can be misleading.

## Workflow

1. Generate the individual enrichment results first.
2. Standardize term identifiers and term descriptions.
3. Select the result sets to compare.
4. Run the co-enrichment module.
5. Inspect shared and unique terms and their direction/strength where the module provides those metrics.
6. Export the underlying comparison table rather than relying only on the figure.

::: {.callout-tip}
For cross-experiment comparisons, term IDs are more reliable join keys than descriptions because descriptions can change between database versions.
:::
